title: Whole Grain Pasta with Tomato Sauce (Home Recipe)

content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain pasta is made from whole wheat flour that retains the bran and germ, providing more fiber and nutrients than refined pasta. The tomato sauce is prepared from ripe tomatoes, onion, garlic, and aromatic herbs. This home recipe combines the nutritional benefits of whole grains with the rich flavor of tomatoes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain pasta contains about twice the fiber of regular white pasta.
Tomatoes are a great source of lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that becomes more bioavailable after cooking.
In Italy, whole grain pasta is known as "pasta integrale" and is used in traditional tomato‑based dishes.
Homemade tomato sauce typically relies on the natural sweetness of ripe tomatoes rather than added sugar.
When cooking whole grain pasta, using a larger pot of water helps prevent sticking.

items.title: High in Fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Complex Carbohydrates
items.content: Provides sustained energy, making it suitable for athletes and active individuals.

items.title: Lycopene and Antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes supply lycopene, which may reduce the risk of heart disease and certain cancers.

items.title: B‑Vitamins
items.content: Whole grain pasta is rich in B1, B3, and B6 vitamins that support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Contains magnesium, iron, and zinc, important for muscle function and immune health.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Wheat pasta contains gluten and is not suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Acidity of Tomato Sauce
items.content: The acidity may trigger heartburn in individuals with gastritis; moderate consumption is advised.

items.title: Sodium Content
items.content: If salt is added to the sauce, monitor overall sodium intake, especially for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pasta hot, tossed with the tomato sauce. Add a drizzle of olive oil, grated Parmesan, fresh basil, or vegetables for extra flavor. For a lighter option, cook the whole grain pasta al dente.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep dry pasta in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked sauce can be refrigerated for up to 3 days or frozen for up to 2 months.
